sections.heading: Our Process for PVC Roofing in Orange, NJ

c.v: Newark Quality Roofing inspects an Orange roof for grease, oil, and chemical exhaust, then checks the slope and ponding before specifying PVC.

runs.v: A low-slope roof needs at least ¼ inch per foot of slope to drain, and ponding held more than 48 hours counts as a defect, per the NRCA and ARMA, so a crew installs tapered insulation to positive drainage.

c.v: Newark Quality Roofing prepares the deck, files a permit, and confirms the recover-versus-tear-off path.

runs.v: A PVC recover proceeds only when the existing roof carries fewer than 2 layers and is not water-soaked, per N.J.A.C. 5:23-6.4 and the NJ Rehabilitation Subcode, and incompatible material such as polystyrene insulation comes out before the membrane goes down.

c.v: Newark Quality Roofing hot-air-welds the PVC field seams and the prefabricated accessories, then probe-tests every weld for full fusion.

runs.v: A crew welds the field laps, factory-fabricated flashings, curb wraps, and pipe boots at penetrations, re-fuses any seam that fails the probe test rather than patching with adhesive, per the NRCA technical library, and documents the completed job for the owner and any insurer.

sections.heading: Is PVC Roofing Any Good? Pros, Disadvantages, and Long-Term Value

items.v: yes, for flat roofs that carry grease, chemicals, rooftop traffic, or ponding. PVC membranes are primarily a flat and low-slope roofing solution.

PVC naturally resists animal fats, oils, and harsh chemicals; PVC roofing handles standing water better than many traditional materials; PVC sheets are hot-air welded together at the seams, which fuse into one continuous sheet; PVC roofing materials are inherently fire-resistant; and PVC requires minimal upkeep outside of routine inspections.

cool roof technology reflects solar energy to reduce heat absorption, and white PVC membranes reflect a high percentage of solar heat, roughly 70 to 85% of solar radiation measured per ASTM C1549, with thermal emittance near 80 to 90%, per the Cool Roof Rating Council. Per the U.S. EPA, the heat-island effect makes daytime air in U.S. urban areas about 1 to 7 degrees Fahrenheit higher than outlying areas, so a reflective membrane improves energy efficiency on a large Orange low-slope roof, and behind a parapet the white sheet does not change a building's curb appeal.
PVC roofing systems can last approximately 20 to 30 years with proper care, which gives long-term value on the investment; proper installation and maintenance are critical for PVC roofing longevity.

PVC costs more to install than TPO or EPDM, plasticizers migrate and stiffen the sheet over decades, PVC cannot touch asphalt or polystyrene materials without a separator, and repairs need a hot-air welder rather than tape.

asphalt shingles need at least a 2:12 slope, so Orange homeowners with a flat porch or rear-addition roof below asphalt shingle roofing or metal roofing on the main slopes can use a membrane such as PVC on the flat section, where the PVC flashing ties into the siding, gutters, and chimney. Architectural shingles provide a layered, three-dimensional look on those main slopes, a new roof can last over 30 years with proper maintenance depending on the material, new roofs can improve home resale value in NJ, and a roof replacement can enhance energy efficiency and curb appeal.

faqs.q: Why is PVC specified for Orange restaurant and food-service buildings?

runs.v: PVC resists the grease, animal fats, and oils in kitchen exhaust that soften and degrade EPDM and TPO, per the NRCA technical library. On Main Street and downtown Orange restaurant roofs, grease leaves an oily film around exhaust fans, and PVC's chemical resistance keeps the membrane intact where that discharge contacts the roof.

faqs.q: How long does a PVC roof last on an Orange commercial or loft building?

runs.v: 20 to 30 years, with thicker reinforced membranes reaching the longer end, per the Single Ply Roofing Industry; PVC outlasts TPO at 7 to 20 years and matches the upper range of EPDM at 15 to 25 years, per the InterNACHI life-expectancy chart.

faqs.q: Does a commercial PVC roof in Orange require a permit?

runs.v: Yes, when the job replaces the roof or repairs more than 25% of the roof area in 12 months on a commercial, multi-family, or attached building, per N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7; a detached one- or two-family reroof is generally ordinary maintenance under the same rule. Confirm with the City of Orange Township construction office before work.

faqs.q: Can PVC be welded over an existing Orange flat roof?

runs.v: Only when the existing covering carries fewer than 2 layers and is not water-soaked, per N.J.A.C. 5:23-6.4; a survey confirms the layer count, moisture, and substrate compatibility, and incompatible material is removed first.

faqs.q: Does a PVC roof on an Orange historic-district property need extra approval?

runs.v: It can: properties in a locally designated historic district can need extra review before exterior roofing work, separate from the construction permit. Confirm a parcel's status with the City of Orange Township before work begins.
